title: QuorumConfig
description:
Multi-agent quorum configuration (planner + delegates).

A quorum consists of a planner agent that decomposes tasks and one or more
delegate agents that execute them. The planner uses the `delegate` built-in
tool to assign work.

```toml
[quorum]
cwd = "."
delegation = true

[planner]
provider = "anthropic"
model = "claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929"
tools = ["delegate", "read_tool", "shell"]

[[delegates]]
id = "coder"
provider = "anthropic"
model = "claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929"
tools = ["edit", "write_file", "shell", "read_tool", "glob"]
```

mcp.description: MCP servers available to all agents in the quorum.

planner.description:
The planner agent that decomposes tasks and delegates to workers.
Should have the `"delegate"` tool enabled.

delegates.description: Delegate (worker) agents that execute tasks assigned by the planner.

mesh.description: Optional kameo libp2p mesh for cross-machine delegation.

remote_agents.description:
Remote agents on other mesh nodes available for delegation.
Requires `[mesh] enabled = true`.

dotagents.description: Optional `.agents` Protocol loading settings (disabled by default).

QuorumSettings.description: Top-level settings for a multi-agent quorum (planner + delegates).

cwd.description: Working directory for the quorum. Relative paths are resolved against this.

delegation.description: Enable task delegation from the planner to delegate agents. Default: `true`.

verification.description: Enable verification pass after delegation completes. Default: `false`.

snapshot_policy.description:
Snapshot policy for capturing file state during delegation.
- `"diff"`: Capture file diffs between snapshots.
- `"metadata"`: Capture file metadata only.
- absent / `null`: No snapshots.

delegation_summary.description:
Optional LLM call that summarises the planner conversation before
handing off to a delegate, providing richer context.

delegation_wait_policy.description:
How to handle multiple concurrent delegations completing.
- `"any"` (default): proceed when the first delegate finishes.
- `"all"`: wait for all delegates to finish.

delegation_wait_timeout_secs.description: Timeout in seconds to wait for delegations to complete. Default: `120`.

delegation_cancel_grace_secs.description:
Grace period in seconds to allow in-flight delegates to finish after
the wait policy threshold is met. Default: `5`.

max_parallel_delegations.description: Maximum number of delegates that can run in parallel. Default: `5`.

workspace.description:
Managed Git worktree workspaces (`[quorum.workspace]`). One service is
shared by the planner and every delegate. Disabled by default.

repository_knowledge.description:
Portable repository knowledge (`[quorum.repository_knowledge]`). One
service is shared across the quorum. Disabled by default.

DelegationSummaryConfig.description:
Configuration for delegation summary LLM call
This generates an Implementation Brief from the parent planning conversation
before delegation to provide context to the coder agent

provider.description: LLM provider for the summary call (can be different from main agent)

model.description: Model for the summary call (should be cheap/fast, e.g., claude-haiku)

api_key.description: API key override (optional, falls back to env)

enabled.description: Enable/disable (default: true when config section present)

max_tokens.description: Maximum tokens for the summary (prevents runaway context consumption)

timeout_secs.description: Timeout in seconds for the summarizer LLM call (default: 30)

min_history_tokens.description:
Minimum estimated tokens in parent history before triggering LLM summarization.
Below this, raw formatted history is injected directly (no LLM call).
Default: 2000 (~8000 chars / ~10-15 messages)

WorkspaceSettings.description:
Managed Git worktree workspace settings (`[agent.workspace]` /
`[quorum.workspace]`).

Settings only *enable the capability* and tune how a requested worktree is
built. Isolation itself stays an explicit per-request decision: an option-less
session is local whether or not the service is enabled.

```toml
[agent.workspace]
enabled = true
# storage_root = "~/.qmt/worktrees"   # relative paths resolve against the config file
# baseline = "commit"                 # "commit" | "current_working_tree"
```

enabled.description: Build a workspace service. Default `false`: no service, behavior unchanged.

storage_root.description:
Durable storage root for managed checkouts. Defaults to
`<qmt config dir>/worktrees` (`~/.qmt/worktrees`). A leading `~/` is
expanded; relative paths resolve against the config file.

baseline.description:
Default baseline for explicitly requested top-level isolation that does
not choose one itself. It never decides *whether* to isolate. Delegates
always start from the parent's working contents.

BaselineMode.description: What the baseline of a new isolated workspace is captured from.

oneOf.description:
Capture a committed ref only. Uncommitted local edits in the source
are excluded and disclosed.

Capture the source's current working contents (tracked working files,
tracked deletions, and non-ignored untracked files) into an immutable
private baseline without touching the source index, HEAD, or files.

RepositoryKnowledgeSettings.description:
Portable repository knowledge settings (`[agent.repository_knowledge]` /
`[quorum.repository_knowledge]`).

The feature is **disabled by default**. Only host configuration can enable
it; a repository file (`.qmt/knowledge.toml`) selects *what* to index but can
never enable the feature, grant tools, or widen filesystem access.

```toml
[agent.repository_knowledge]
enabled = true
# root = "."                  # explicit knowledge root (required for non-Git workspaces)
# max_files = 2000
# max_file_bytes = 524288
# max_total_bytes = 33554432
# max_response_bytes = 16384  # capped at 64 KiB
# force_hash = false          # hash every selected file on every refresh

[agent.repository_knowledge.delivery]
# Both automatic delivery stages are independently opt-in.
# orientation = false
# index_context = false
```

enabled.description:
Build a repository knowledge service. Default `false`: no repository
reads, writes, tools, or prompt changes.

root.description:
Explicit knowledge root. When absent, the Git worktree root containing
the session working directory is used. Relative paths resolve against
the config file. Non-Git workspaces require this to be set.

allowed_roots.description:
Host allowlist of roots repository knowledge may read from. When empty
no extra restriction applies; when non-empty, a resolved root outside
every listed directory is denied. Relative paths resolve against the
config file.

max_files.description: Maximum number of selected files indexed per refresh.

max_file_bytes.description: Maximum size in bytes of any single selected file.

max_total_bytes.description: Maximum total bytes indexed across all selected files.

max_response_bytes.description:
Default serialized response budget in bytes for repository tools.
Capped at 64 KiB.

default_result_limit.description: Default result limit for `repo_knowledge_query`. Capped at 50.

force_hash.description:
Hash every selected file during reconciliation, bypassing the
metadata fast path (debugging aid).

allow_ignored.description: Include Git-ignored files matched by the manifest. Default `false`.

delivery.description: Automatic delivery controls. Each stage is independently opt-in.

RepositoryKnowledgeDeliverySettings.description:
Automatic delivery controls. Both stages default off and are independent of
each other and of tool availability.

orientation.description: Prompt-triggered orientation cards before the first model request.

index_context.description: Knowledge-for-path context after successful built-in `index` calls.

max_cards.description: Maximum cards delivered per turn (default 2, capped at 4).

max_tokens.description: Maximum estimated tokens delivered per turn (default 600, capped at 2000).

max_bytes.description: Serialized hard ceiling per turn in bytes (default 4 KiB, capped at 16 KiB).

McpServerConfig.description:
MCP (Model Context Protocol) server configuration.

The `transport` field is the discriminator — it must be `"stdio"` or `"http"`.
Note: the field is named `transport`, NOT `type`.

**stdio** — spawns a local process:
```toml
[[mcp]]
name = "filesystem"
transport = "stdio"
command = "npx"
args = ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem", "/tmp"]
```

**http** — connects to a remote MCP endpoint:
```toml
[[mcp]]
name = "context7"
transport = "http"
url = "https://mcp.context7.com/mcp"
headers = { AUTHORIZATION = "Bearer ${CONTEXT7_API_KEY}" }
```

**http + OAuth** — the login flow runs through the `_querymt/auth/*`
extension using the provider id `mcp:<name>`:
```toml
[[mcp]]
name = "linear"
transport = "http"
url = "https://mcp.linear.app/mcp"
auth = { type = "oauth", scopes = ["read"] }
```

**http over a Unix socket** (Unix only; `url` is used for addressing):
```toml
[[mcp]]
name = "local"
transport = "http"
url = "http://localhost/mcp"
socket_path = "/run/mcp.sock"
```

Both transports accept `tasks = true` (declare the MCP tasks extension;
default `false`) and `cache = false` (disable response caching of tool
listings; default `true`).

To enable MCP tools, add them to `agent.tools`:
- `"filesystem.*"` — all tools from the `filesystem` server
- `"filesystem.read_file"` — a specific tool from the server

Build values in Rust with [`McpServerConfig::stdio`] / [`McpServerConfig::http`]
and the `with_*` setters; the variants are `#[non_exhaustive]`.

oneOf.description: Local process-based MCP server launched via stdio.

name.description: Unique name for this server. Referenced in `agent.tools` as `"name.*"`.

env.description:
Environment variables to set for the server process.
Supports `${VAR}` interpolation.

tasks.description: Declare the MCP tasks extension to this server (default `false`).

cache.description: Honour server cache hints for tool listings (default `true`).

oneOf.description: Remote HTTP-based MCP server.

name.description: Unique name for this server. Referenced in `agent.tools` as `"name.*"`.

url.description: Full URL of the MCP HTTP endpoint.

headers.description:
HTTP headers to include in every request (e.g. auth tokens).
Supports `${VAR}` interpolation in values.

auth.description:
OAuth authorization. Cannot be combined with `socket_path` or an
`Authorization` header.

socket_path.description: Connect over this Unix domain socket instead of TCP (Unix only).

tasks.description: Declare the MCP tasks extension to this server (default `false`).

cache.description: Honour server cache hints for tool listings (default `true`).

McpAuth.description: Authorization scheme for an HTTP MCP server.

oneOf.description:
OAuth 2.1 with discovery, PKCE and (unless `client_id` is set) dynamic
client registration.

client_id.description: Pre-registered client id. When absent, dynamic registration is used.

redirect_port.description: Loopback redirect port. Defaults to a fixed port.

strict_scopes.description:
Refuse grants wider than `scopes` (default `false`).

Authorization servers may grant more than was requested. With
`strict_scopes = true` a login whose token carries any scope beyond
`scopes` (plus `offline_access`) is discarded, and stored
credentials with such a grant are not used to connect. Checked
against the token response `scope` and, for JWT access tokens, the
`scope` / `scp` claim. Requires a nonempty `scopes`.

PlannerConfig.description:
Planner agent configuration.

The planner decomposes tasks and delegates subtasks to worker agents.
It should have the `"delegate"` built-in tool enabled.

model.description: Model identifier for the planner (typically a capable reasoning model).

tools.description:
Tools available to the planner. The `"delegate"` tool is required for
task delegation. Typical set: `["delegate", "read_tool", "shell", "glob"]`.

mode.description: Initial mode of new planner sessions: `build` (default), `plan` or `review`.

system.description:
System prompt for the planner. Accepts a string or mixed array of
inline strings and `{ file = "path" }` references.

parameters.description: Extra parameters forwarded to the LLM provider API.

middleware.description: Middleware stack for the planner (limits, context management, etc.).

execution.description: Execution policy (tool output, pruning, compaction, snapshot, rate limit).

ToolSpec.description: Tool selector: `name` (built-in or provider tool), `server.tool` (one MCP tool) or `server.*` (every tool of an MCP server).

AgentMode.description:
Runtime operating mode for the agent.
Modes control what the agent is allowed to do and what system reminders are injected.

oneOf.description: Full read/write mode - all tools available, no restrictions
Planning mode - read-only, agent observes and plans without making changes
Review mode - read-only, agent reviews code and provides feedback

CacheHint.description:
Cache hint for providers that support prompt caching.
When set on a message, the provider may use it to mark cache breakpoints,
allowing the conversation prefix up to this point to be cached and reused.

oneOf.description:
Ephemeral cache breakpoint. Providers that support caching (e.g., Anthropic)
will cache the conversation prefix up to and including this message.
The optional TTL requests a supported lifetime in seconds; providers
validate/translate it, sometimes at request scope. None uses their default.
This is not a deletion deadline or a guarantee of cache availability.
Unsupported endpoints may ignore hints without changing message content.

MiddlewareEntry.description:
A middleware entry in the agent's processing stack.

The `type` field selects which middleware to use; all other fields are
forwarded to that middleware as configuration.

Available middleware types:
- `"limits"` — hard cap on steps and turns (`max_steps`, `max_turns`)
- `"context"` — token-window management (`warn_at_percent`, `compact_at_percent`, `fallback_max_tokens`)
- `"dedup_check"` — detects repeated/similar code output (`threshold`, `min_lines`)
- `"agent_mode"` — build/plan/review mode switching (`default`, `reminder`, `review_reminder`)
- `"plan_mode"` — legacy read-only mode (prefer `agent_mode`)

```toml
[[middleware]]
type = "limits"
max_steps = 200
max_turns = 50

[[middleware]]
type = "context"
warn_at_percent = 80
compact_at_percent = 90
```

type.description:
The middleware type name. Built-in types: `"limits"`, `"context"`,
`"dedup_check"`, `"agent_mode"`, `"plan_mode"`, `"parallel_edit_guard"`,
`"output_limit_recovery"`.
Custom middleware types can be registered at runtime.

ExecutionPolicy.description:
Execution-policy configuration (3-layer context management system).

- **Layer 1** `tool_output`: Truncates individual tool outputs exceeding
  size limits. Saves overflowed content to temp storage.
- **Layer 2** `pruning`: Removes old tool output entries from the context
  window after every turn to reclaim token budget.
- **Layer 3** `compaction`: AI-powered summarisation triggered when the
  context window fills. Condenses history to free space.

Also controls `snapshot` (undo/redo via git), `rate_limit` (429 retry), and
whether an unfinished finite task forces an additional model request.

```toml
[agent.execution.tool_output]
max_lines = 2000
max_bytes = 51200

[agent.execution.pruning]
protect_tokens = 40000

[agent.execution.compaction]
auto = true

[agent.execution.snapshot]
backend = "git"
```

pruning.description: Pruning settings — runs after every turn (Layer 2)

compaction.description: AI compaction settings — runs on context overflow (Layer 3)

task_completion_guard.description: Force one additional model request when a finite task remains active.

max_stop_recoveries.description:
Maximum times middleware may turn a stop into a continuation within one
turn before the stop is published (default: 5).

max_stop_hook_continuations.description:
Maximum times a Stop hook may turn the end of a turn into another agent
step within one turn (default: 1). `0` makes Stop hooks advisory only.

overflow_storage.description: Where to save full output when truncated

OverflowStorage.description: Where to store overflow output when tool output is truncated

oneOf.description: Discard overflow (don't save)
Save to temp directory (/tmp/qmt-tool-outputs/{session_id}/)
Save to persistent data directory

PruningConfig.description: Configuration for pruning (Layer 2) - runs after every turn

protect_tokens.description: Tokens of recent tool outputs to protect from pruning

minimum_tokens.description: Minimum tokens to clear before pruning (avoids small pruning operations)

protected_tools.description: Tools that should never be pruned

CompactionConfig.description: Configuration for AI compaction (Layer 3) - runs on context overflow

auto.description: Enable/disable AI compaction (setting true auto-enables ContextMiddleware)

provider.description: Optional: different provider for compaction (cheaper model)

model.description: Optional: different model for compaction (cheaper model)

retry.description: Retry configuration for compaction LLM calls

RetryConfig.description: Retry configuration for compaction LLM calls

SnapshotBackendConfig.description:
Configuration for snapshot backend (undo/redo support).

Snapshots capture the state of modified files before each agent action,
enabling undo/redo. Requires the `[agent.execution.snapshot]` section.

```toml
[agent.execution.snapshot]
backend = "git"
# Optional retention. Leave both unset to never delete snapshots.
# max_snapshots = 100
# max_age_days = 30
```

backend.description:
Snapshot storage backend.
- `"git"`: Commits snapshots into the current git repository.
- `"none"`: Snapshots disabled (default).

max_snapshots.description:
Maximum number of snapshots to retain; oldest are pruned first. Unset
(the default) means no limit. Must be at least 1.

max_age_days.description:
Maximum age of snapshots in days; older ones are pruned. Unset (the
default) means no limit. Must be at least 1.

RateLimitConfig.description: Configuration for rate limit retry behavior

max_retries.description: Total request-attempt budget, including the initial request (default: 3)

default_wait_secs.description: Default wait time in seconds if no retry-after header (default: 60)

backoff_multiplier.description:
Backoff multiplier when no retry-after header (default: 2.0)
Wait time increases exponentially: default_wait_secs * multiplier^(attempt-1)
Must be finite and `> 0`.

max_stream_retries.description:
Maximum stream recreations within the shared request-attempt budget (default: 2).
Each recreation restarts the provider request and also consumes `max_retries`.

jitter_ratio.description:
Proportional jitter for calculated delays (`0.0..=1.0`). Provider retry
hints are not jittered.

Runtime-only for now: not written into `session_execution_configs` so older
qmtcode builds (strict `deny_unknown_fields`) can still open sessions.
TODO(session-compat): drop `skip_serializing` and persist once older readers
are retired, or gate behind a session config migration.

max_wait_secs.description:
Upper bound for every retry delay (`>= 1`).

Provider `Retry-After` / message hints are clamped by this field before
sleeping or emitting retry-wait events.

Runtime-only for now — same session-compat rationale as `jitter_ratio`.
TODO(session-compat): persist with `jitter_ratio` when ready.

include_external.description: Check external paths (Claude Code, agents conventions)

urls.description: Remote skill URLs (Phase 2 - not yet implemented)

mcp.description: Offer skills published by connected MCP servers (default: true)

oneOf.description: Automatically allow (default)
Block entirely
Prompt user for confirmation

PermissionsConfig.description:
`[agent.permissions]`, `[planner.permissions]` and `[delegates.permissions]`.

```toml
[agent.permissions]
ask         = ["shell"]             # prompt; "Allow for this session" offered
always_ask  = ["ibkr.place_order"]  # prompt on every call
timeout_sec = 120                   # reject unanswered prompts; unset = wait
```

ask.description:
Tools that need the user's approval. The prompt offers "Allow once",
"Allow for this session" and "Reject".

always_ask.description:
Tools that prompt on every call and never offer the session option.
Wins over `ask`.

timeout_sec.description:
Seconds after which an unanswered approval prompt (from a list or a
hook) is rejected. Prompts wait indefinitely when unset.

DelegateConfig.description:
Delegate (worker) agent configuration.

Delegates execute tasks assigned by the planner. Each delegate has its own
tool set, system prompt, and optionally its own MCP servers.

id.description: Unique identifier for this delegate, used by the planner to target it.

description.description: Human-readable description shown to the planner when choosing a delegate.

capabilities.description:
Capability tags used by the planner to select suitable delegates
(e.g. `["coding", "filesystem", "gpu"]`).

tools.description:
Tools available to this delegate. Typical coder set:
`["edit", "write_file", "shell", "read_tool", "glob", "search_text"]`.

mode.description: Initial mode of new delegate sessions: `build` (default), `plan` or `review`.

system.description:
System prompt for this delegate. Accepts a string or mixed array of
inline strings and `{ file = "path" }` references.

parameters.description: Extra parameters forwarded to the LLM provider API.

mcp.description: MCP servers specific to this delegate (in addition to quorum-level MCP).

middleware.description: Middleware stack for this delegate (limits, context management, etc.).

execution.description: Execution policy (tool output, pruning, compaction, snapshot, rate limit).

peer.description:
Optional mesh peer name (references a `[[mesh.peers]]` entry).

When set, LLM calls for this delegate are routed to the remote peer via
the mesh while tool execution continues locally on the planner node.
This is the "remote model, local session" pattern.

Requires `[mesh] enabled = true`. Validated at startup.

isolation.description:
Workspace isolation for tasks delegated to this delegate.

Precedence: an explicit non-`inherit` value on the `delegate` tool call,
then this value, then the parent's execution mode. `isolated` requires
`[quorum.workspace] enabled = true`.

DelegationIsolation.description: Delegation isolation requested for a delegate relative to its parent.

oneOf.description:
Resolve from the parent's execution mode: isolated parents isolate
delegates by default; local parents keep legacy shared execution.
Explicitly share the parent's checkout (disclosed as shared).
Explicitly request a private checkout for this delegate.

MeshTomlConfig.description:
Configuration for the kameo libp2p mesh.

In TOML:
```toml
[mesh]
enabled = true
listen = "/ip4/0.0.0.0/tcp/0"
discovery = "mdns"

[[mesh.peers]]
name = "dev-gpu"
addr = "/ip4/192.168.1.100/tcp/9000"
```

enabled.description: Whether to start the mesh swarm at startup.  Default: `false`.

listen.description: Multiaddr to listen on.  Default: `"/ip4/0.0.0.0/tcp/0"` (OS-assigned random port).

transport.description:
Transport layer.  Default: `"lan"`.

Set to `"iroh"` for internet-capable mesh with NAT traversal and relay.
Requires the `remote` feature.

iroh_gso.description:
Enable Generic Segmentation Offload (GSO) on the shared iroh actor endpoint.
Default: true. Set to false as a UDP offload compatibility workaround.
Applies to all Iroh scopes; does not affect LAN or separate payload endpoints.

iroh_dns.description:
DNS policy for the shared iroh endpoint; absent preserves upstream defaults.
Disabling public DNS fallback does not disable N0's public pkarr services.

auto_fallback.description:
Whether `provider_node_id = None` may fall back to mesh provider discovery.

Default: `false` (local-only unless an explicit `provider_node_id` is set).

peers.description: Explicit peers to connect to at startup.

request_timeout_secs.description:
Timeout in seconds for non-streaming mesh request-response calls
(e.g. compaction, no-tools LLM calls).  Default: 300 (5 minutes).
Increase for very slow models or large context windows.

stream_reconnect_grace_secs.description:
Grace period (seconds) to wait for mesh reconnection before failing an
in-flight remote streaming request.

identity_file.description:
Path to the persistent ed25519 identity file.

When absent, defaults to `~/.qmt/mesh_identity.key`.  The node's
`PeerId` is derived from this keypair and stays stable across restarts.

invite.description:
Invite token to join an existing mesh.

When set, the node bootstraps in "join" mode: it dials the inviter
from the token using the iroh transport.  Overrides `transport` to
`"iroh"` automatically.

Supports `${VAR}` interpolation, e.g. `"${QMT_MESH_INVITE}"`.

Example:
```toml
[mesh]
enabled = true
invite = "${QMT_MESH_INVITE}"
```

node_name.description:
Human-readable name advertised to mesh peers.

When set, overrides the OS hostname in `GetNodeInfo` responses.
Useful on mobile where the OS hostname is often meaningless ("unknown").

lan.description:
LAN transport sub-configuration (new multi-transport syntax).

When present and `enabled = true`, the LAN transport is activated
alongside any Iroh scopes.  Takes precedence over the legacy
`transport` and `discovery` fields for LAN configuration.

iroh.description:
Iroh mesh scopes (new multi-transport syntax).

Each entry represents a logical Iroh mesh scope.  When present and
at least one entry has `enabled = true`, the Iroh transport is
activated alongside LAN (if also enabled).

MeshDiscoveryConfig.description:
Discovery strategy for the libp2p swarm.

In TOML: `discovery = "mdns"` | `"kademlia"` | `"none"`.

oneOf.description: Zero-config local-network discovery (mDNS multicast).
Distributed discovery using the Kademlia DHT (for cross-subnet).
No automatic discovery — peers are added only via `[[mesh.peers]]`.

MeshTransportConfig.description:
Transport layer for the libp2p swarm.

In TOML: `transport = "lan"` | `"iroh"`.

oneOf.description: Traditional TCP + QUIC + Noise + Yamux (LAN-optimised, default).

iroh-backed QUIC transport with relay and NAT traversal (internet-capable).
Requires the `remote` feature.

fallback_nameservers.description: An empty list preserves upstream's public fallback resolvers.

MeshPeerConfig.description:
A single peer that this node should connect to in the mesh.

In TOML:
```toml
[[mesh.peers]]
name = "dev-gpu"
addr = "/ip4/192.168.1.100/tcp/9000"
```

addr.description: libp2p multiaddr of the peer, e.g. `"/ip4/192.168.1.100/tcp/9000"`.

LanMeshTomlConfig.description:
LAN mesh sub-configuration for multi-transport setups.

In TOML:
```toml
[mesh.lan]
enabled = true
discovery = "mdns"
listen = "/ip4/0.0.0.0/tcp/0"
```

enabled.description: Whether the LAN transport is enabled.

listen.description:
Multiaddr to listen on for LAN connections.

Falls back to `[mesh] listen` when absent.

IrohMeshTomlConfig.description:
Iroh mesh scope sub-configuration for multi-transport setups.

In TOML (array of tables):
```toml
[[mesh.iroh]]
enabled = true
invite = "..."
name = "personal"
```

enabled.description: Whether this Iroh scope is enabled.

invite.description:
Invite token string to join an existing Iroh mesh.

When set, the `mesh_id` is derived from the invite grant.
Supports `${VAR}` interpolation.

name.description:
Human-readable name for this Iroh scope.

Used as the `mesh_id` when `invite` is absent, or as a display
label alongside the invite-derived mesh_id.

RemoteAgentConfig.description:
A remote agent running on another mesh node, used for task delegation.

Remote agents require `[mesh] enabled = true` and a matching peer in
`[[mesh.peers]]`. This is for multi-machine agent delegation — it is
NOT for MCP tool servers (use `[[mcp]]` for those).

```toml
[mesh]
enabled = true

[[mesh.peers]]
name = "dev-gpu"
addr = "/ip4/192.168.1.100/tcp/9000"

[[remote_agents]]
id = "gpu-coder"
name = "GPU Coder"
description = "Coder running on GPU server with fast model"
peer = "dev-gpu"
capabilities = ["gpu", "fast-model"]
```

id.description: Unique agent identifier used when targeting this agent for delegation.

name.description: Human-readable display name shown in delegation context.

description.description:
Short description of the agent's purpose or specialisation,
shown to the planner when choosing which agent to delegate to.

peer.description:
Name of the peer in `[[mesh.peers]]` that hosts this agent.
Must match the `name` field of a `[[mesh.peers]]` entry.

capabilities.description:
Capability tags used by the planner to select suitable agents
(e.g. `["gpu", "shell", "filesystem"]`).

DotagentsSettings.description:
Opt-in protocol configuration.

The default is disabled, preserving all existing TOML-only and programmatic
behavior. Roots and workspace are only consulted when `enabled = true`.

global_enabled.description: Whether the global layer is enabled.

workspace_enabled.description: Whether the workspace layer is enabled.

trusted_roots.description: Additional roots trusted by confined resolution.

workspace_task_trust.description: Trust policy for repository-controlled workspace repeat tasks.

DotagentsStrictness.description:
How strictly the loader treats error diagnostics during resolution.

This controls whether an error diagnostic is fatal for the resolved
configuration as a whole, or whether unaffected valid entries remain
available. Runtime activation (see the runtime adapters) additionally uses
this to decide whether construction fails or continues with warnings.

oneOf.description:
Activate valid entries, return structured warnings, and fail only when
the selected root configuration cannot be applied safely.
Fail resolution when any error diagnostic is present.

DotagentsTaskTrustPolicy.description: Host policy for workspace protocol tasks.

oneOf.description: Ask the host and remain pending when no approval mechanism exists.
Never activate workspace protocol tasks.
Activate without approval. This is intentionally and explicitly unsafe.
